prompt: A checkout path requires a gateway, authentication service and payment service. All component states are independent, each service sometimes works and sometimes fails, and there are no other failure causes. How does adding a fourth required service with these properties affect path availability?

options.text: It reduces availability if the added service can fail independently.
options.explanation: Success now requires an additional component to be working.

options.text: It improves availability by adding redundancy.
options.explanation: A required dependency is not an alternative replica.

options.text: It leaves availability equal to the least available service.
options.explanation: Independent additional failure opportunities make the full path less available than each imperfect component.
All four can still be up together.

workedExample: Write the success condition in words: every required service must be up. A new required dependency removes some formerly successful states, so it cannot improve availability in this model.

link.title: Introduction to Probability — Grinstead and Snell

prompt: A colleague estimates redundant-replica downtime by multiplying individual downtime probabilities. Any working replica is sufficient, with ideal failover. Which conditions undermine the independence assumption? Select all that apply.

options.text: One bad configuration is deployed everywhere together.
options.explanation: A shared software cause can synchronise failures.

options.text: Failure of one replica overloads the others.
options.explanation: A first failure changes the other replicas’ failure chances.

options.text: Downtimes follow the stated mutually independent model.
options.explanation: That is the assumption needed for multiplying their probabilities.

options.text: All replicas share one power feed.
options.explanation: A common power failure can take them down together.

workedExample: The product model needs each replica’s failure chance to remain unchanged when another fails. Shared causes and load cascades violate that requirement. Spreading infrastructure may reduce some shared causes but does not remove every one.
